title: O Love, Who Formedst Me to Wear
description: O Love, Who Formedst Me to Wear in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Johann Scheffler wrote these words in German. Catherine Winkworth's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 348.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Love, who for-medst me to wear The i-mage of Thy God-head here; Who sought-est me with ten-der care Through all my wand’-rings wild and drear,— O Love, I give my-self to Thee, Thine ev-er, on-ly Thine, to be.

lines: O Love, who formedst me to wear
The image of Thy Godhead here;
Who soughtest me with tender care
Through all my wand’rings wild and drear,—
O Love, I give myself to Thee,
Thine ever, only Thine, to be.
O Love, who ere life’s earliest dawn
On me Thy choice hast gently laid;
O Love, who here as man wast born
And like to us in all things made,—
O Love, I give myself to Thee,
Thine ever, only Thine, to be.
O Love, who once in time wast slain,
Pierced through and through with bitter woe;
O Love, who, wrestling thus, didst gain
That we eternal joy might know,—
O Love, I give myself to Thee,
Thine ever, only Thine, to be.
O Love, of whom in truth and light,
The Word and Spirit, life and power,
Whose heart was bared to them that smite,
To shield us in our trial hour,—
O Love, I give myself to Thee,
Thine ever, only Thine, to be.
O Love, who thus hast bound me fast
Beneath that gentle yoke of Thine;
Love, who hast conquered me at last,
Enrapturing this heart of mine,—
O Love, I give myself to Thee,
Thine ever, only Thine, to be.
O Love, who lovest me for aye,
Who for my soul dost ever plead;
O Love, who didst my ransom pay,
Who for me e’er dost intercede,—
O Love, I give myself to Thee,
Thine ever, only Thine, to be.
O Love, who once shalt bid me rise
From out this dying life of ours;
O Love, who once above yon skies
Shalt set me in the fadeless bowers,—
O Love, I give myself to Thee,
Thine ever, only Thine, to be.

licence: Public domain: Johann Scheffler died in 1677; Catherine Winkworth died in 1878.
credits: Words by Johann Scheffler (1624–1677), translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
